content_html:
Complexity ↔ Simplicity

Every system begins with a set of simple rules: in physics, a few fundamental forces and constants generate the entire cosmos; in biology, DNA’s four bases yield the diversity of life; in consciousness, neurons firing in simple patterns give rise to thought, perception, and memory. This is the creative phase of a cycle - simplicity unfolds into complexity through interaction, feedback, and differentiation.

Out of the simple, the complex arises; out of repetition, pattern; out of order, chaos.

This mirrors the emergent property of systems - where interactions among simple elements produce results that no single part contains. At a certain point however, systems become too intricate - overgrown, entangled, or self-referential. Ecologies reach saturation, where new species struggle to find niches, the mind becomes cluttered with memories and abstractions, and societies over-complicate through bureaucracy and technology. Here complexity becomes opaque - it begins to obscure rather than reveal meaning.

When the branches grow too dense, sunlight no longer reaches the roots.

This marks the turning point in the cycle - the necessity for simplification, pruning, or renewal. Eventually, systems collapse, adapt, or simplify: forest fires clear undergrowth for new life. In cognition, sleep, meditation, or forgetting prune neural connections. In mathematics or philosophy, abstraction leads back to elegant unifying principles. This return to simplicity is not regression but integration - complexity distilled into essence.

Simplicity after complexity is not the same as simplicity before it.

It mirrors the entropy cycle - complexity disperses, leaving behind refined structure or insight. From this new simplicity, the cycle begins again. New systems, ideas, or forms emerge - not identical, but more evolved. What was once “complex” becomes the new “simple” foundation. Thus, simplicity and complexity are phases of one rhythm, not opposites. The universe, the mind, and life itself breathe through this rhythm - expansion and contraction, differentiation and synthesis.

Imagine a taiji (yin–yang) symbol:

The black (simplicity) contains a white seed (potential for complexity).
The white (complexity) contains a black seed (return to simplicity).

It’s a self-sustaining loop: Simplicity → Complexity → Simplicity. Each turn reveals a deeper layer of the same pattern - fractal simplicity emerging within complexity.

  • Encoding starts simple (stimulus → trace).
  • Through association and learning, complexity builds (networks of meaning).
  • Through forgetting and consolidation, simplicity returns (essence retained, noise pruned).

Thus, memory itself cycles - from sparse impressions to rich associations to distilled understanding. Knowledge matures not by adding more, but by knowing what can be left out.

Phase Process Natural Analogy Cognitive Analogy Symbolic Polarity
Simplicity → Generative rules, potential Seed germination Perception & encoding Yin
Complexity ↑ Growth, differentiation Ecosystem expansion Association & learning Yang
Dissolution ↓ Simplification, entropy Fire / decay Forgetting & sleep Yin
Renewal → Rebirth of simplicity Regrowth Insight / wisdom Yang → Yin
